summary: Sir Willoughby Jones, 3rd Baronet, MP for Cheltenham 1847–48, grandson of Capt. Effingham Lawrence; John's 5th cousin 6 times removed.
bio:
Willoughby Jones was born on 24 November 1820, the second son of Major-General Sir John Thomas Jones, 1st Baronet, and Catharine Maria Lawrence, a daughter of Capt. Effingham Lawrence; through the Lawrences he was John's 5th cousin six times removed. He was educated at Eton and Trinity College, Cambridge. He inherited the baronetcy in 1845 when his elder brother Sir Lawrence Jones, 2nd Baronet, a travel writer, was murdered in Turkey, and from July 1847 he sat as Member of Parliament for Cheltenham.

His deaf daughter Maud drew the interest of Alexander Graham Bell, and his son the Rt. Rev. Herbert Jones became Bishop of Lewes. Sir Willoughby died on 21 August 1884.

media.note: Sir Willoughby Jones 3rd Baronet (24 November 1820 – 21 August 1884) was a Norfolk landowner and an  English Conservative Party politician.  He was briefly Member of Parliament (MP) for the Cheltenham constituency.
